automation.title: Automation Rules
automation.description: Rules that run automatically on deals. Each rule watches one stage of one pipeline and, once a deal has stayed in it for the set number of hours, unassigns the deal so it returns to the pool.

when.pipeline: When a deal is in pipeline

automation.summary: When a deal stays in {pipeline} › {stage} for {duration}, then:

conflicts.incomplete: “{rule}” needs a stage and a stay time of at least 1 hour.
conflicts.beforeLimit: “{rule}” unassigns deals after {hours}h, before the stage “{stage}” stay limit of {limit}h — the overdue alert will never appear for that stage.
conflicts.unreachable: “{blocked}” can never run: “{by}” ({hours}h) already acts first on the same deals. Make one rule more specific with an earlier time, or deactivate one.

automation.howItWorks: Rules are checked automatically every 10 minutes. The clock starts when the deal entered the stage, or when someone last assigned it — whichever is later — so reassigning a deal gives it a fresh window. Deals that are already unassigned are skipped. Unassigning a deal also unassigns its lead, the same as any reassignment. Closed stages (Won, Competitor, Archive) can't have rules. A note counts only if it was written by the currently assigned user after that clock started; the comment written when moving a deal between stages doesn't count. Stay time counts working hours only: Fridays and Saturdays (Cairo time) are not counted, so a deal that entered a stage on Thursday morning has stayed about 24 hours by Sunday morning, not 72. The clock starts at 11:59 AM on a working day: a deal that enters before 11:59 AM starts counting at 11:59 AM (at 11:30 AM its stay time is still zero), one that enters after 5:00 PM starts the next working day at 11:59 AM, and one that enters on a Friday or Saturday starts on Sunday at 11:59 AM.

integrations.keysDescription: Keys let other software create leads in Acropol. Each key is shown only once, when it is created.
integrations.keyNameHint: What will use this key, e.g. "Website form".
integrations.assignToHint: Optional. Leads created with this key go to this person; otherwise they arrive unassigned.

integrations.apiDescription: Send a request for each new lead. Authenticate with an API key.
integrations.apiAuth: Send the key as "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" (or an "X-API-Key" header).
integrations.apiResponses: Responses: 201 = lead created; 200 with status "duplicate" = that phone number already belongs to a lead or customer (nothing is created, the existing record is returned); 400 = invalid data; 401 = missing or invalid key.
integrations.whatsappDescription: Every WhatsApp message sent to your business number creates a lead for the sender.
integrations.waStep1: In Meta for Developers → your app → WhatsApp → Configuration, set the Callback URL above and a Verify token of your choice.
integrations.waStep3: Put the same verify token and the app secret (App settings → Basic) in the server environment, then restart:
integrations.waBehaviour: The sender's WhatsApp name and first message become the lead's name and notes, with source WhatsApp. If the number already belongs to a lead or customer, no new lead is created. Requests are verified with Meta's signature, so only Meta can post here. The URL must be public HTTPS.
integrations.waVerifyTokenHint: Any text you choose; paste the same one into the webhook setup in Meta.
integrations.waSecretSaved: A secret is saved. Leave empty to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
integrations.waSecretFromEnv: The secret comes from the server settings. Enter one here to replace it.
integrations.coexDescription: Connect your business number once. It keeps working in the WhatsApp Business app on your phone, and Acropol receives every message and makes a lead for each new person.
integrations.coexStep1: Save the Meta app id, the Embedded Signup configuration id, and the app secret above.
integrations.coexStep2: Press Connect and sign in to Facebook, then choose your WhatsApp Business app number.
integrations.coexStep3: On the phone, confirm the connection in the WhatsApp Business app when asked.
integrations.coexNeedSecret: Save the app secret in the WhatsApp section above first.
integrations.coexConnectedNoWebhook: Connected, but Acropol could not subscribe to messages. Press Connect again, or check the app in Meta.
integrations.coexDisconnectConfirm: Disconnect {number}? Acropol stops receiving its messages. The number keeps working in the WhatsApp Business app.
